title: Vivekananda in America
hook: should wisdom have a price? a rented room, and no tickets
tomorrow: a week of guests and hosts. which line goes home with you?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vivekananda in America walked away from a tour that sold him as a novelty. Today, where he taught instead, and one question.

A good teacher can charge by the minute now: a course, a subscription, a paywall right before the best part. So here's the question: should wisdom have a price? Vivekananda answered with a room in New York. Rented, plain, and crowded. Not enough chairs, so people sat on the floor. No ticket at the door.
screen: `A PAYWALL BEFORE THE BEST PART.` → `SHOULD WISDOM HAVE A PRICE?` → `A ROOM WITH NO TICKETS.`

segments.voice: His disciples' biography describes it simply. In New York he rented rooms and taught classes free of charge. He taught Vedanta, the teaching of the Upanishads, and he taught it as practice: how to sit, how to breathe, how to watch the mind. Out of those classes grew his book Raja Yoga, and a small circle that became the Vedanta Society of New York. He had just walked away from being sold. In this room, he didn't sell the teaching either. A hall holds a crowd for one evening; a room holds the same people week after week. A neighbor tradition says something close, in its own words. In the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus sends out his disciples to heal and to preach, and tells them: "freely ye have received, freely give." Shared: both treat what was received as a gift, so it goes out as a gift. And an honest difference. In Matthew, the disciples are sent out on the road to proclaim the kingdom of heaven, carrying no gold, and the homes that take them in feed them. Vivekananda stayed put, rented a room, and taught a way of sitting with the mind. The same open hand, on a different road.
screen: `FREE CLASSES IN A RENTED ROOM.` · `VEDANTA, TAUGHT AS PRACTICE.` · `MATTHEW: FREELY GIVE.` · `SHARED HAND, DIFFERENT ROAD.`

segments.voice: If there's paper near you, write down the name of one person who taught you something and never asked anything back. If there isn't, trace the name with a finger on your palm. Then sit with it, and let the gift stay a gift.
Vivekananda in America: in New York, free classes in a rented room, and the start of the Vedanta Society.
Your line: Vivekananda in America. A hall holds a crowd; a room holds students. Rest well tonight.
